chunks.text: 28-year-old male, Unemployed, resident of Ang Mo Kio, Singapore.
Left distal radius fracture (age 16, fully healed)
General Anesthesia with Single-shot Spinal Anesthesia for Surgical Procedure

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Liew, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your surgery today. I'd like to go through a few things with you to make sure everything is in order for your laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia with spinal block. Can you please confirm your current medications and if there have been any changes since your last review?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure, doctor. I'm still on Metformin 500mg twice a day and Sitagliptin 100mg once a day for my diabetes. I used to take Loratadine for my nose, but I stopped it because it was getting too expensive. Now I take Montelukast 10mg once a day instead. Oh, and I also take Omeprazole 20mg once a day, but I think I stopped that a while back too.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for that update, Mr. Tan. It's important we have the most current information. You mentioned stopping Omeprazole — was that due to any specific reason or just discontinuation? Also, have you had any new allergic reactions to medications recently?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No specific reason for stopping Omeprazole, just thought I didn't need it anymore, lah. But yes, actually, I had a reaction to some antibiotic I took recently. I went to the polyclinic for a UTI and they gave me Cefuroxime. After a few days, I developed a rash all over my body. It was pretty bad, so I had to stop it and switch to another antibiotic.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I see. So to confirm, you now have a known allergy to Cefuroxime in addition to your previous allergy to Penicillin, which caused a rash. Is that correct?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, exactly. Both caused rashes, so I guess I should avoid both.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Absolutely. We'll make sure that's clearly noted in your chart. Now, regarding your diabetes, how well-controlled is it? Are you having any issues with your blood sugar levels?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: It's been pretty stable, doctor. I check my sugar levels a few times a week, and they're usually within the normal range. I haven't had any episodes of high or low sugar recently.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. And how about your mobility and overall fitness? Are you able to walk, climb stairs, or do any regular physical activity?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I can walk around, but I do get a bit short of breath if I walk too fast or climb too many stairs. I'm not as active as I used to be, but I can still do daily activities without too much trouble.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? If so, were there any complications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first time having surgery. I've never had anesthesia before, so I'm a bit nervous about it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's completely normal. We'll make sure you're comfortable and safe throughout the process. Finally, have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I followed the instructions. I had my last meal around 7pm last night and only sipped water until 8pm. Nothing since then.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. We'll proceed with the plan for general anesthesia combined with spinal anesthesia to minimize pain during and after surgery. We'll also ensure your diabetes and allergies are carefully managed. Any questions or concerns before we begin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. Thank you, doctor.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] fluid bolus: five hundred milliliters of balanced crystalloid

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:25] notable event: mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty five mmHg, treated with phenylephrine ten micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:40] maintenance fluid: one hundred milliliters per hour of normal saline

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:55] notable event: transient bradycardia to forty five bpm, treated with atropine zero point six milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm okay, I guess. Still a bit groggy, but I can talk.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Can you tell me your pain level out of 10? Any discomfort from the incisions or inside your abdomen?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: It's about a 4, maybe 5. There's some tightness and soreness, but not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, we can manage that with pain relief. Are you feeling nauseous or did you feel sick at all during or after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, no nausea. Just a bit thirsty, but I know I can't drink yet, right?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's correct for now. How's your breathing? Any tightness or difficulty breathing?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is fine. I'm a bit more conscious of my tummy, but I can breathe okay.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Since you had general anesthesia with a spinal, do you remember anything from the operating room?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Not really. I remember going to sleep, then waking up here. Nothing in between.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's expected. You have a BMI of 28.5 and are diabetic — are you feeling any signs of low sugar, like shakiness or dizziness?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don't feel shaky. I'm just tired, but that's probably normal after surgery.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. We'll keep an eye on your blood sugar and get you moving soon. Any other concerns?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. Thanks for checking on me.
